topics.name: Inversion of Control (IoC) & Dependency Injection (DI)
topics.summary: Follow a Spring bean from registration through injection, use, and cleanup.

subTopics.name: What is IoC and why Spring uses it
subTopics.summary: Let the container assemble objects and manage their lifecycle while application classes focus on behavior.

subTopics.name: What problem does DI solve?
subTopics.summary: Pass collaborators in so production code can swap implementations and tests can use fakes.

subTopics.name: How Spring creates and injects beans internally
subTopics.summary: Track how Spring registers definitions, resolves dependencies, initializes objects, and can wrap them in proxies.

subTopics.name: ApplicationContext vs BeanFactory
subTopics.summary: Compare the basic BeanFactory with ApplicationContext and its additional startup and application services.

subTopics.name: Eager vs Lazy loading - When to use which?
subTopics.summary: Delay an expensive bean when useful, and predict when an eager dependency will still create it at startup.

subTopics.name: Bean Scopes (Singleton, Prototype, Request, Session, Application)
subTopics.summary: Choose scope by deciding who shares an instance and when it should be released.

subTopics.name: Why prototype beans don't get destroyed automatically?
subTopics.summary: Spring initializes prototypes but leaves their later cleanup to whoever obtains them.

subTopics.name: Bean Lifecycle (@PostConstruct, @PreDestroy)
subTopics.summary: Use PostConstruct after dependency injection and PreDestroy during managed shutdown where the scope supports it.

subTopics.name: Complete bean lifecycle steps
subTopics.summary: Trace definition registration, construction, injection, initialization, post-processing, and destruction.

subTopics.name: Bean Initialization and Destruction callbacks
subTopics.summary: Compare annotation callbacks, lifecycle interfaces, and configured init or destroy methods.

subTopics.name: Aware Interfaces (BeanNameAware, ApplicationContextAware)
subTopics.summary: Use an Aware callback when a bean truly needs its container-supplied name or context.

subTopics.name: Configuration Styles: Java-based (@Configuration), Annotation-based (@Component), XML
subTopics.summary: Compare factory methods, component scanning, and XML as ways to register bean definitions.

subTopics.name: Dependency Injection types: Constructor (WHY preferred) vs Setter vs Field (WHY discouraged)
subTopics.summary: Use constructor injection for required dependencies and setters for optional configuration where appropriate.

subTopics.name: Autowiring modes and @Qualifier usage
subTopics.summary: Narrow matching beans with a qualifier and distinguish modern annotation injection from older XML modes.

subTopics.name: @Primary vs @Qualifier
subTopics.summary: Primary supplies a preferred default. A qualifier narrows which candidates can satisfy an injection point.

topics.name: Spring Bean Management
topics.summary: Register beans deliberately and choose the right extension point for customization.

subTopics.name: @Component, @Service, @Repository, @Controller
subTopics.summary: Use stereotypes to signal a general component, business service, persistence adapter, or web controller.

subTopics.name: Why @Repository exists (exception translation)
subTopics.summary: Repository marks persistence code and can participate in translating supported provider exceptions.

subTopics.name: @Configuration vs @Component
subTopics.summary: Configuration marks a source of bean definitions. Component marks a type eligible for scanning.

subTopics.name: @Bean vs @Component
subTopics.summary: Use Bean for an explicit factory method and Component for types registered through scanning.

subTopics.name: Bean Naming Strategies
subTopics.summary: Give beans explicit names when needed and understand how generated names can collide.

subTopics.name: Lazy vs Eager Initialization
subTopics.summary: Create required singletons early or delay a bean when the startup tradeoff is worth it.

subTopics.name: @DependsOn annotation
subTopics.summary: DependsOn expresses initialization order when there is no direct injected dependency.

subTopics.name: BeanFactoryPostProcessor vs BeanPostProcessor
subTopics.summary: Change definition metadata with a factory post-processor and wrap instances with a bean post-processor.

subTopics.name: Real-time use cases for BeanPostProcessor and BeanFactoryPostProcessor
subTopics.summary: Compare editing bean definitions before creation with wrapping initialized objects for cross-cutting behavior.

topics.name: Autowiring & Bean Resolution
topics.summary: Predict how Spring chooses a dependency and diagnose ambiguity or cycles.

subTopics.name: How Spring resolves dependency when multiple beans of same type
subTopics.summary: Start with candidates of the requested type, then consider qualifiers, primary status, and applicable name matching.

subTopics.name: @Autowired working internally
subTopics.summary: Spring processes injection metadata and resolves candidate beans through the container.

subTopics.name: Optional Injection with @Autowired
subTopics.summary: Compare optional injection through required=false, Optional, or a nullable parameter.

subTopics.name: Circular Dependency - Constructor vs Setter injection case
subTopics.summary: Constructor cycles prevent construction. Setter cycles may be resolvable in some configurations but are better redesigned.

subTopics.name: Why constructor injection fails for circular dependency
subTopics.summary: Two constructors cannot each receive the other fully created object first. Break the cycle with clearer responsibilities.

topics.name: Spring Expression Language (SpEL)
topics.summary: Use small expressions to select and transform configuration values.

subTopics.name: SpEL basics and syntax
subTopics.summary: Read SpEL syntax for literals, operators, property access, and simple expressions.

subTopics.name: Using SpEL with @Value
subTopics.summary: Use #{...} for an expression and ${...} for a configuration placeholder.

subTopics.name: Accessing beans, properties, collections via SpEL
subTopics.summary: Navigate bean properties and collections or select particular elements in an expression.

topics.name: Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP)
topics.summary: Put shared behavior around method calls and understand where proxy boundaries matter.

subTopics.name: What is AOP? Why needed?
subTopics.summary: Use AOP to apply recurring behavior around selected calls without copying it into every method.

subTopics.name: Cross-cutting concerns (Logging, Transaction management)
subTopics.summary: Apply concerns such as transaction handling and logging consistently across services.

subTopics.name: Aspect, Advice, Pointcut, JoinPoint
subTopics.summary: A pointcut selects join points, advice supplies behavior, and an aspect groups the two.

subTopics.name: Types of Advice (Before, After, Around, AfterReturning, AfterThrowing)
subTopics.summary: Choose advice based on whether it runs before, after, or around the call and whether the call succeeds.

subTopics.name: Annotations: @Before, @After, @Around (MOST IMPORTANT), @AfterReturning, @AfterThrowing
subTopics.summary: Use Around when advice must control if or when the original invocation proceeds.

subTopics.name: Pointcut expressions execution(), within()
subTopics.summary: Match method execution or calls on types using the pointcut designators Spring supports.

subTopics.name: Proxy Mechanism - JDK Dynamic Proxy vs CGLIB
subTopics.summary: JDK proxies expose interfaces. Class-based proxies subclass eligible types.

subTopics.name: Why interface-based proxy preferred?
subTopics.summary: Interface proxies keep callers on the interface contract. Class proxies fit APIs that require concrete types.

subTopics.name: Self-invocation problem in Spring AOP
subTopics.summary: A call on this stays inside the target and bypasses proxy advice.

subTopics.name: Transaction & AOP relation
subTopics.summary: Transaction advice opens, joins, commits, or rolls back work around a proxied invocation.

subTopics.name: Why @Transactional uses AOP
subTopics.summary: The proxy interprets transaction metadata before and after a call crosses the proxy boundary.

subTopics.name: Why private methods don't work with @Transactional
subTopics.summary: A private method cannot be intercepted by the ordinary Spring transaction proxy.

topics.name: Spring Events
topics.summary: Publish application events to decouple the sender from interested listeners.

subTopics.name: ApplicationEvent and ApplicationListener
subTopics.summary: Publish an event through the context and register a listener for its type.

subTopics.name: Custom Events
subTopics.summary: Model an event as a small object that carries the data its recipients need.

subTopics.name: @EventListener annotation
subTopics.summary: Use EventListener on a bean method to subscribe to matching application events.

topics.name: Spring Profiles & Environment
topics.summary: Use profiles to choose beans and property sources to choose configuration values.

subTopics.name: @Profile usage
subTopics.summary: Register a bean only when matching profile conditions are active.

subTopics.name: Environment abstraction
subTopics.summary: Read active profiles and resolved configuration through Environment.

subTopics.name: PropertySource and Property resolution
subTopics.summary: Spring resolves property keys across ordered sources, with higher-precedence values winning.

topics.name: Spring MVC Architecture
topics.summary: Trace a request from the front controller to its handler and response.

subTopics.name: DispatcherServlet workflow (VERY COMMON)
subTopics.summary: DispatcherServlet selects a handler adapter for the mapped handler and dispatches the request.

subTopics.name: Front Controller Pattern
subTopics.summary: A single front controller coordinates request handling across multiple controllers.

subTopics.name: HandlerMapping role
subTopics.summary: HandlerMapping uses request information to locate an appropriate handler and related interceptors.

subTopics.name: Controller, ViewResolver, Model
subTopics.summary: A controller can return model data and a view name. A resolver locates the view to render.

topics.name: Controller Development
topics.summary: Map requests to methods and bind each input from the right part of HTTP.

subTopics.name: @Controller vs @RestController
subTopics.summary: Controller commonly renders views. RestController writes return values to the response body by default.

subTopics.name: @RequestMapping vs @GetMapping, @PostMapping
subTopics.summary: Use general RequestMapping or choose a shortcut restricted to a specific HTTP method.

subTopics.name: @PathVariable vs @RequestParam
subTopics.summary: PathVariable reads a URI segment. RequestParam reads a named request parameter.

subTopics.name: @RequestBody vs @ResponseBody
subTopics.summary: RequestBody deserializes the input body. ResponseBody writes the return value to the outgoing body.

subTopics.name: @RequestBody vs @ModelAttribute
subTopics.summary: Use RequestBody for a serialized payload and ModelAttribute to bind request values to an object.

topics.name: Data Binding & Validation
topics.summary: Bind request input, validate it, and report errors where the caller can fix them.

subTopics.name: @ModelAttribute
subTopics.summary: ModelAttribute exposes a value to the model and can bind request data onto it.

subTopics.name: @ModelAttribute lifecycle
subTopics.summary: Spring can obtain or create an attribute, bind request data, and run validation before invoking the handler.

subTopics.name: BindingResult
subTopics.summary: Place BindingResult next to the bound argument when the handler should inspect its errors.

subTopics.name: JSR-380 Bean Validation (@NotNull, @Size, @Email)
subTopics.summary: Express field constraints such as NotNull, Size, and Email and trigger validation at the boundary.

subTopics.name: Custom validators
subTopics.summary: Add a validator when a rule depends on several fields or needs a domain-specific check.

topics.name: Exception Handling
topics.summary: Turn known failures into consistent responses without duplicating error handling.

subTopics.name: @ExceptionHandler
subTopics.summary: Map a particular exception type to a response or view in a handler method.

subTopics.name: @ControllerAdvice
subTopics.summary: Use ControllerAdvice to share exception handlers and other controller support across controllers.

subTopics.name: @ExceptionHandler vs @ControllerAdvice
subTopics.summary: ExceptionHandler defines the handler method. ControllerAdvice makes shared handlers available beyond one controller.

subTopics.name: Global vs local exception handling
subTopics.summary: Handle controller-specific cases locally and share common response behavior through advice.

subTopics.name: Global Exception Handling Strategy and Best Practices
subTopics.summary: Return consistent status codes and error bodies while keeping internal exception details out of public responses.

topics.name: View Technologies
topics.summary: Choose how MVC resolves a view name into the final HTML page.

subTopics.name: JSP integration
subTopics.summary: Configure a JSP view resolver and confirm that the selected deployment supports JSP.

subTopics.name: Thymeleaf basics
subTopics.summary: Use a Thymeleaf template to render model attributes into HTML on the server.

subTopics.name: ViewResolver configuration
subTopics.summary: Map logical view names to concrete templates with resolver prefixes, suffixes, and order.

topics.name: Spring JDBC
topics.summary: Run JDBC queries with Spring's resource management, row mapping, and error translation.

subTopics.name: JdbcTemplate
subTopics.summary: JdbcTemplate runs SQL and manages common connection, statement, and result-set handling.

subTopics.name: RowMapper
subTopics.summary: Use RowMapper to turn each result row into a domain object.

subTopics.name: ResultSetExtractor
subTopics.summary: Use ResultSetExtractor when mapping needs access to the entire result set, such as grouped parent and child rows.

subTopics.name: Exception translation
subTopics.summary: Spring can wrap provider-specific SQL failures in portable DataAccessException subclasses.

topics.name: Spring ORM & JPA Integration
topics.summary: Use managed entities and plan how related data is fetched inside a unit of work.

subTopics.name: JPA integration with Spring
subTopics.summary: Spring integrates JPA persistence contexts and entity managers with managed transactions.

subTopics.name: EntityManager vs Session
subTopics.summary: EntityManager is the standard JPA API. Session is Hibernate's provider-specific API.

subTopics.name: @PersistenceContext
subTopics.summary: Use PersistenceContext to get a managed EntityManager reference.

subTopics.name: Lazy vs Eager loading
subTopics.summary: Fetch associations when needed and keep the persistence context lifecycle in mind.

subTopics.name: N+1 problem (VERY COMMON)
subTopics.summary: An initial query followed by one query per parent is an N+1 pattern. Confirm it in the SQL trace.

topics.name: Transaction Management
topics.summary: Choose transaction boundaries, then predict what commits, rolls back, or joins existing work.

subTopics.name: What is transaction management?
subTopics.summary: A transaction groups operations into a unit with a defined commit or rollback outcome.

subTopics.name: Declarative vs Programmatic Transactions
subTopics.summary: Declare boundaries with annotations or wrap specific code using a transaction template.

subTopics.name: @Transactional annotation
subTopics.summary: Transactional tells Spring the requested transaction behavior at an eligible boundary.

subTopics.name: @Transactional working internally
subTopics.summary: In proxy mode, an eligible call reaches transaction advice before it enters the target method.

subTopics.name: Propagation and Isolation levels
subTopics.summary: Propagation decides which transaction runs the method. Isolation controls visibility between transactions.

subTopics.name: Propagation types (REQUIRED, REQUIRES_NEW, etc.)
subTopics.summary: Required joins or starts a transaction. RequiresNew starts a separate one and suspends an existing transaction where supported.

subTopics.name: Rollback rules
subTopics.summary: Configure rollback rules to match failures that should undo the work.

subTopics.name: Rollback - Checked vs Runtime exception
subTopics.summary: By default, Spring generally rolls back for unchecked exceptions and errors. Configure checked exceptions if required.

subTopics.name: Why @Transactional doesn't work on private methods
subTopics.summary: Private methods cannot be intercepted by ordinary transaction proxies.

subTopics.name: Why @Transactional doesn't work on internal method calls
subTopics.summary: Calls from a method to another method on the same target bypass ordinary transaction proxy advice.

topics.name: Exception Handling
topics.summary: Understand which persistence failures Spring translates and how callers should handle them.

subTopics.name: DataAccessException hierarchy
subTopics.summary: DataAccessException provides an unchecked hierarchy for common data access failures.

subTopics.name: Checked vs Runtime exceptions in Spring
subTopics.summary: Spring's data access exceptions are unchecked. Configure transaction rules when a checked failure should roll back.

topics.name: Core Concepts
topics.summary: Trace identity, permissions, and request processing through Spring Security.

subTopics.name: Authentication vs Authorization
subTopics.summary: Authentication establishes identity. Authorization checks whether that identity may perform an action.

subTopics.name: SecurityContext & SecurityContextHolder
subTopics.summary: SecurityContext holds the current authentication. SecurityContextHolder gives code access to that context.

subTopics.name: SecurityFilterChain & Filters
subTopics.summary: A matching SecurityFilterChain runs a configured sequence of security filters for the request.

subTopics.name: Filter order importance
subTopics.summary: Identity must be established before later authorization checks can make the intended decision.

subTopics.name: UserDetailsService & PasswordEncoding (BCrypt)
subTopics.summary: Load user details and use a password encoder such as BCrypt to verify stored password hashes.

subTopics.name: UserDetailsService flow
subTopics.summary: A provider loads user details, checks credentials, and creates an authenticated result on success.

topics.name: Authentication Mechanisms
topics.summary: Compare credential handling, browser login, and token-based request authentication.

subTopics.name: Basic Auth & Form Login
subTopics.summary: HTTP Basic sends credentials with requests. Form login typically authenticates once and uses a session.

subTopics.name: JWT (JSON Web Tokens): Implementation & Best Practices
subTopics.summary: Treat a JWT as untrusted until its signature and expected claims have been validated.

subTopics.name: Stateless vs Stateful authentication
subTopics.summary: Session-based authentication stores per-user state on the server. Stateless processing authenticates each request independently.

topics.name: OAuth2 & OpenID Connect (OIDC)
topics.summary: Keep the OAuth roles straight and distinguish delegation from identity.

subTopics.name: Resource Server, Authorization Server, Client
subTopics.summary: The authorization server issues tokens, the resource server protects APIs, and the client requests access.

subTopics.name: Social Login (Google, GitHub)
subTopics.summary: Use OAuth login with a provider. OpenID Connect adds an identity layer where the provider supports it.

topics.name: Authorization
topics.summary: Map permissions to roles or authorities and check them at the right boundary.

subTopics.name: Role-based vs Authority-based access
subTopics.summary: Use roles for groups of permissions and authorities for the actual grants checked by the application.

subTopics.name: Role vs Authority
subTopics.summary: A role is conventionally an authority with a role prefix. An authority can represent a finer-grained permission.

subTopics.name: hasRole vs hasAuthority
subTopics.summary: HasRole commonly applies a role prefix. HasAuthority checks the supplied authority string directly.

subTopics.name: Method Level Security (@PreAuthorize, @PostAuthorize)
subTopics.summary: Use PreAuthorize before invocation and PostAuthorize to check a returned result where appropriate.

topics.name: Protection
topics.summary: Distinguish browser cross-origin access rules from requests made with automatically sent credentials.

subTopics.name: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)
subTopics.summary: CORS headers tell a browser whether scripts from another origin may read a response.

subTopics.name: CORS - browser vs server perspective
subTopics.summary: The server returns CORS headers. The browser enforces them, including preflight checks when required.

subTopics.name: CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery)
subTopics.summary: CSRF protection prevents unintended state changes sent with credentials the browser attaches automatically.

subTopics.name: CSRF - what, why, when to disable
subTopics.summary: Base the CSRF decision on how credentials are sent. Cookie-authenticated endpoints still need protection.

topics.name: Spring Container & Initialization
topics.summary: Follow container startup from discovering definitions to creating and initializing beans.

subTopics.name: How Spring container starts
subTopics.summary: The context loads definitions, applies factory post-processors, and prepares eligible singleton beans.

subTopics.name: ClassPath scanning
subTopics.summary: Component scanning looks for candidate classes under configured base packages.

subTopics.name: Reflection usage in Spring
subTopics.summary: Spring uses reflection and metadata to discover and invoke constructors, methods, and annotations.

topics.name: Design Principles & Best Practices
topics.summary: Use dependency boundaries and state ownership to keep services testable and safe to share.

subTopics.name: Why Spring prefers interfaces
subTopics.summary: A service that depends on an interface can accept alternate implementations and test doubles.

subTopics.name: Immutable beans and thread safety
subTopics.summary: Prefer immutable or stateless shared services and protect any mutable state that multiple threads can reach.

subTopics.name: Memory impact of singleton beans
subTopics.summary: Singleton instances retain their reachable state for the life of the container unless released.

topics.name: Spring Events
topics.summary: Send an application event and decide which components should react to it.

subTopics.name: ApplicationEvent and ApplicationListener
subTopics.summary: Publish an event through Spring and handle it with an ApplicationListener for the relevant type.

subTopics.name: Custom Events
subTopics.summary: Use a focused event object to carry the context that interested components need.

subTopics.name: @EventListener annotation
subTopics.summary: Register a bean method with EventListener to react to events of a matching type.

topics.name: Spring Profiles & Environment
topics.summary: Select behavior by environment without spreading deployment checks through business code.

subTopics.name: @Profile usage
subTopics.summary: Use Profile to include a bean or configuration only in selected environments.

subTopics.name: Environment abstraction
subTopics.summary: Use Environment to inspect active profiles and retrieve resolved properties.

subTopics.name: PropertySource and Property resolution
subTopics.summary: Trace the same key through competing sources to understand why one value was selected.
